issue.title: [Bug]: event-bus-redis and workflow-engine-redis loaders turn a failed Redis connect into an unhandled rejection ("Connection is closed.") and log it as established
issue.body:
### Package.json file

```JSON
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@medusajs/event-bus-redis": "2.21.2",
    "@medusajs/workflow-engine-redis": "2.21.2",
    "ioredis": "5.11.1"
  }
}
```

The same code is in 2.22.1 and on `develop` (efcfb5ab2982b26d18daeedfa2e9624d0db2edf2).

### Node.js version

v24

### Database and its version

n/a (Redis/Valkey connection)

### Operating system name and version

Linux

### Browser name

_No response_

### What happended?

The Redis loaders of `event-bus-redis` and `workflow-engine-redis` connect like this:

```ts
await new Promise(async (resolve) => {
  await connection.connect(resolve)
})
```

- [`packages/modules/event-bus-redis/src/loaders/index.ts#L37-L39`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/efcfb5ab2982b26d18daeedfa2e9624d0db2edf2/packages/modules/event-bus-redis/src/loaders/index.ts#L37-L39)
- [`packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/loaders/redis.ts#L150-L152`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/efcfb5ab2982b26d18daeedfa2e9624d0db2edf2/packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/src/loaders/redis.ts#L150-L152) (`getConnection`, used for 4 connections)

When the first connect fails, for example when the TCP connect exceeds `connectTimeout` (`connect ETIMEDOUT`) while the app boots before Redis is reachable, two things go wrong:

1. `connect(resolve)` passes the error to the callback as a value. The outer promise resolves, the surrounding `try/catch` never sees an error, and the loader logs "Connection to Redis … established".
2. The `await connection.connect(...)` inside the `async` executor still rejects with `Connection is closed.` Nothing observes the promise returned by an `async` Promise executor, so this becomes an **unhandled rejection**. Error trackers report it as an unhandled error with no application frames. Without a `process.on("unhandledRejection")` listener, Node ≥ 15 terminates the process.

The clients also have no `error` listener, so the `ETIMEDOUT` itself is printed as `[ioredis] Unhandled error event`.

ioredis keeps reconnecting afterwards, so the client recovers once Redis answers. The problem is the unhandled rejection and the misleading log line.

**Minimal reproduction** (no Medusa needed, only `ioredis@5.11.1`; `10.255.255.1` is a non-routable address, so the TCP connect times out):

```js
// repro.js — node repro.js
const IORedis = require("ioredis")
process.on("unhandledRejection", (e) => {
  console.log("UNHANDLED REJECTION:", e.stack.split("\n").slice(0, 2).join("\n"))
  process.exit(1)
})
const connection = new IORedis("redis://10.255.255.1:6379", {
  maxRetriesPerRequest: null,
  enableReadyCheck: false,
  lazyConnect: true,
  connectTimeout: 500,
})
;(async () => {
  try {
    const r = await new Promise(async (resolve) => {
      await connection.connect(resolve)
    })
    console.log("loader went on, resolve() got:", r && r.message)
  } catch (err) {
    console.log("loader caught:", err.message) // never reached
  }
})()
```

Output:

```
[ioredis] Unhandled error event: Error: connect ETIMEDOUT
    at Socket.<anonymous> (…/ioredis/built/Redis.js:183:41)
    …
loader went on, resolve() got: Connection is closed.
UNHANDLED REJECTION: Error: Connection is closed.
    at EventEmitter.connectionCloseHandler (…/ioredis/built/Redis.js:220:28)
```

### Expected behavior

A failed initial connect is caught by the loader's own `try/catch` and logged as "An error occurred while connecting to Redis …". No unhandled rejection is raised.

Any of these would fix it:

```ts
await connection.connect()
```

```ts
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => connection.connect().then(resolve, reject))
```

Adding `connection.on("error", …)` (logging through the module logger) would also stop the `[ioredis] Unhandled error event` output.

### Actual behavior

- The loader logs "Connection to Redis in module 'event-bus-redis' established" (or the `workflow-engine-redis` equivalent) although the connect failed.
- An unhandled rejection `Error: Connection is closed.` is raised from `EventEmitter.connectionCloseHandler` (`ioredis/built/Redis.js`).
- Error tracking reports it as an unhandled error with only system frames.

### Link to reproduction repo

The snippet above is self-contained (`npm i ioredis@5.11.1 && node repro.js`).

issue.title: [Bug]: buyget promotions apply the discount to items with is_discountable: false
issue.body:
### Package.json file
Reproduced inside the medusajs/medusa monorepo on develop at 396aa3f510 (@medusajs/promotion 2.21.2). The relevant code is unchanged in the published 2.21.x packages. No custom package.json involved; the repro below runs against the promotion module's own integration test runner.

### Node.js version
v22.22.2

### Database and its version
PostgreSQL 17.5

### Operating system name and version
macOS 15.7.3

### Browser name
Not applicable

### What happended?
A product can be marked as not discountable (product.discountable = false, surfaced on cart items as is_discountable: false). Standard promotions respect that flag: the item filter in the promotion module's compute-actions code skips any line with is_discountable: false, so a 100% standard promotion targeting a gift card produces no adjustment.

Buyget promotions do not. getComputedActionsForBuyGet in packages/modules/promotion/src/utils/compute-actions/buy-get.ts builds its eligible target items with filterItemsByPromotionRules, which only evaluates the target rules and never looks at is_discountable. So a "buy 1 shirt, get 1 gift card at 100%" promotion discounts the gift card to zero even though the merchant marked gift cards as not discountable.

I checked the 8,000-line compute-actions.spec.ts for this module: there is no test with is_discountable: false at all, so nothing guards either path.

### Expected behavior
A buyget promotion never produces an adjustment on an item with is_discountable: false, the same way standard promotions behave. Non-discountable items should still be allowed to satisfy the buy rules (buying a gift card can qualify you for a discounted shirt), they just should not receive the discount.

### Actual behavior
computeActions returns an addItemAdjustment for the non-discountable item:

Context: shirt (is_discountable: true, category catg_shirt, subtotal 1000) and gift card (is_discountable: false, category catg_gift, subtotal 500).

Standard promotion, 100% percentage, target rule items.product_category.id eq catg_gift:
  computeActions(["STD"], context) -> []

Buyget promotion, buy_rules items.product_category.id eq catg_shirt, target_rules items.product_category.id eq catg_gift, 100%, apply_to_quantity 1, buy_rules_min_quantity 1:
  computeActions(["BG"], context) -> [{ action: "addItemAdjustment", item_id: "item_gift_card", amount: 500, code: "BG" }]

### Link to reproduction repo
No separate repo needed, it reproduces directly against PromotionModuleService with the module's own moduleIntegrationTestRunner (packages/modules/promotion/integration-tests):

```ts
const context = {
  currency_code: "usd",
  items: [
    { id: "item_shirt", quantity: 1, subtotal: 1000, original_total: 1000, is_discountable: true,
      product_category: { id: "catg_shirt" }, product: { id: "prod_shirt" } },
    { id: "item_gift_card", quantity: 1, subtotal: 500, original_total: 500, is_discountable: false,
      product_category: { id: "catg_gift" }, product: { id: "prod_gift" } },
  ],
}

await service.createPromotions({
  code: "BG",
  type: "buyget",
  application_method: {
    type: "percentage", target_type: "items", value: 100, allocation: "each",
    max_quantity: 1, apply_to_quantity: 1, buy_rules_min_quantity: 1,
    buy_rules: [{ attribute: "items.product_category.id", operator: "eq", values: ["catg_shirt"] }],
    target_rules: [{ attribute: "items.product_category.id", operator: "eq", values: ["catg_gift"] }],
  },
})

const result = await service.computeActions(["BG"], context)
// expected: []
// actual:   [{ action: "addItemAdjustment", item_id: "item_gift_card", amount: 500, code: "BG" }]
```

Swap type to "standard" with the same target rule and the result is [], which is the behaviour I would expect from buyget too.

issue.title: [Bug]: Product module runs parallel queries inside a transaction (pg client.query() deprecation, fails with pg@9)
issue.body:
### Package.json file

```json
"@medusajs/medusa": "2.21.0",
"@medusajs/framework": "2.21.0",
"pg": "8.23.0"
```

### Node.js version

v22

### Database and its version

PostgreSQL 16

### Operating system name and version

Debian (node:22-slim container)

### What happened?

Every run that creates product categories or product variants logs this warning:

```
DeprecationWarning: Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is deprecated and will be removed in pg@9.0. Use async/await or an external async flow control mechanism instead.
```

Traced with `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-deprecation`, it comes from two places in `@medusajs/product` that run queries **in parallel inside a transaction**, so they all go to the same pg client:

**1. `ProductCategoryRepository.create`** (`packages/modules/product/src/repositories/product-category.ts`, around line 395): a `Promise.all` over the new categories, each one calling `manager.count(...)` for its siblings.

```
at SqlEntityManager.count (@mikro-orm/core/EntityManager.js:1282:23)
at @medusajs/product/src/repositories/product-category.ts:400:31
at async Promise.all (index 2)
at ProductCategoryRepository.create (@medusajs/product/src/repositories/product-category.ts:395:24)
at ProductCategoryService.create (@medusajs/product/src/services/product-category.ts:162:12)
at PostgreSqlConnection.transactional (@mikro-orm/knex/AbstractSqlConnection.js:58:25)
…
at createProductCategoriesStep (@medusajs/core-flows/src/product-category/steps/create-product-categories.ts:36:21)
```

**2. `ProductModuleService.createVariants_`** (`packages/modules/product/src/services/product-module-service.ts`, around line 629): a `promiseAll([...])` of several `list` calls.

```
at AbstractService_.list (@medusajs/utils/src/modules-sdk/medusa-internal-service.ts:230:14)
at async Promise.allSettled (index 0)
at promiseAll (@medusajs/utils/src/common/promise-all.ts:27:18)
at ProductModuleService.createVariants_ (@medusajs/product/src/services/product-module-service.ts:629:7)
at PostgreSqlConnection.transactional (@mikro-orm/knex/AbstractSqlConnection.js:58:25)
…
at ProductModuleService.createProductVariants (@medusajs/product/src/services/product-module-service.ts:606:22)
```

Both patterns are still the same on `develop` as of 2026-09-24.

### Expected behavior

No overlapping queries on a transaction's client. Inside a transaction every query shares one connection, so running them with `Promise.all` gives no concurrency anyway (pg queues them); it only triggers the deprecation. With pg@9 this becomes an error, and creating categories or variants would fail.

A sequential `for … of` with `await` inside the transactional paths would keep the same behaviour without the warning.

### Link to reproduction repo

No public repo. To reproduce with a stock Medusa 2.21 project:

1. Run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-deprecation`.
2. Call `createProductCategoriesWorkflow` with two or more categories under the same parent, or `createProductsWorkflow` with a product that has variants.
3. The warning appears with the stacks above.

issue.title: fix(test-utils): don't signal autovacuum workers when restoring test databases
issue.body:
## Summary

**What** — The test-utils database helpers no longer try to cancel or terminate role-less backends, such as autovacuum workers, when they drop or restore a test database.

**Why** — If the test database role isn't a superuser (for example, it only has `CREATEDB`), `medusaIntegrationTestRunner` can fail at random in `beforeEach` with `permission denied to cancel query`. `cancelAndTerminateDatabaseConnections` and `terminateDatabaseConnections` signal every backend connected to the database. Sometimes an autovacuum worker is on the test database at that moment. It shows up with a NULL `usename` in `pg_stat_activity`, and a non-superuser can't signal it, so the query throws. The retry loop in `dropDatabaseIfExists` only retries on `being accessed by other users`, so the error fails the test. Setups that use the default superuser `postgres` role never see this.

**How** — Added `AND usename IS NOT NULL` to the `pg_cancel_backend` and `pg_terminate_backend` queries in `packages/medusa-test-utils/src/medusa-test-runner-utils/postgres-template.ts`. Superuser runs lose nothing: `DROP DATABASE` and `CREATE DATABASE ... WITH TEMPLATE` already stop autovacuum workers on the databases involved and wait for them to exit.

**Testing** — Added tests to `src/__tests__/postgres-template.spec.ts`. They mock a server that refuses to signal role-less backends, then cover `restorePostgresDatabaseFromTemplate`, `dropPostgresDatabaseTemplate`, and `dropDatabase`. Before the fix, all three rejected with `permission denied to cancel query`. After the fix, they resolve. The spec file (15 tests) and the package's unit suite (8 suites, 69 tests) pass.

---

## Checklist

- [x] I have added a **changeset** for this PR
- [x] The changes are covered by relevant **tests**
- [ ] I have verified the code works as intended locally
- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable

---

## Additional Context

The regression tests mock the pg client, because there's no reliable way to make an autovacuum worker start on a database inside a test. I also tried a representative HTTP integration suite (`integration-tests/http/__tests__/currency`) locally. It failed in the runner's `beforeAll` during app boot, before any template restore ran, so it says nothing about this change either way.

Fixes #17686

issue.title: fix(core-flows): re-price cart shipping methods after promotions are recomputed
issue.body:
A cart that has a promotion applied and a delivery price already set, then another promotion is applied on the shipping price that depends on the cart total, may lead to incorrect totals.

For example, consider a shop where delivery is £4.99 or free on orders of £50 or more (the shipping price has a rule on item_total). Beans cost £12 a bag, and the code WELCOME25 takes 25% off.

Scenario 1:

1. Adds 3 bags. £36, and the discount is saved as a fixed −£9.00, so the cart is £27.
2. Enters their address and picks Standard delivery. It's priced at £4.99, which is correct because £27 < £50.
3. Gets to the checkout summary and changes 3 → 5 bags with the quantity stepper.
4. Medusa re-prices delivery before it recalculates the discount:
   - What delivery sees: 5 × £12 = £60, minus the old £9.00 = £51, so delivery is free.
   - Then the discount is recalculated to 25% of £60 = £15, so the goods total becomes £45.
   - Nothing re-prices delivery after that.
5. Clicks "Place order". They pay £45 with free delivery, even though £45 is under the £50 threshold. The shop loses £4.99.

Scenario 2:

- They start with 8 bags: £96 − £24 = £72, so delivery is free.
- They drop to 6 bags. Delivery sees £72 − the old £24 = £48, so it charges £4.99.
- The correct total is £72 − £18 = £54, which should have shipped free.

This PR fixes it by changing the promotion flow to calculate promotions -> refresh shipping prices (happened outside this flow before) -> calculate promotions again if shipping prices changed

Closes DX-3043

issue.title: [Bug]: @medusajs/caching 2.22.4 imports graphql without declaring it; untagged caching.set throws reading 'parseObjectForEntities'
issue.body:
## Summary

`@medusajs/caching@2.22.4` imports `graphql` (`src/utils/parser.ts:9`) without declaring it as a
dependency. It gets whichever copy the package manager hoists. Since 2.22.4, `@medusajs/utils`
depends on `graphql@^17.0.2` (2.22.2: `^16.14.2`) and builds the schema the caching strategy reads
(`GraphQLUtils.makeExecutableSchema` in `CachingModuleService.onApplicationStart`). In a project
that also has `graphql@16` installed for something else (for example Payload CMS), pnpm hoists 16.x,
so the parser's `isObjectType` comes from 16.x while the schema was built by 17.x.

Outside `NODE_ENV=production`, graphql's realm check throws in `new CacheInvalidationParser(...)`
(`src/utils/strategy.ts:46`). `MedusaModule.onApplicationStart` swallows the rejection
(`packages/core/modules-sdk/src/medusa-module.ts:141`), so the app boots, the strategy never
subscribes to the event bus, and its parser stays `undefined`. Every later `caching.set` without
`tags` then fails in `computeTags` (`src/utils/strategy.ts:112`). With `NODE_ENV=production` the
check is a plain `instanceof`, so nothing throws, but the parser's type map is empty and automatic
tags are silently not computed.

## Versions

- Works: `@medusajs/*@2.22.2` (utils and the hoisted copy are both graphql 16).
- Fails: `@medusajs/*@2.22.4`, pnpm 10.34.6, Node 22, with `graphql@16.14.2` also in the workspace.
- `develop` (checked 2026-11-09): `packages/modules/caching/package.json` still declares no `graphql`.

## Reproduction

In a Medusa 2.22.4 project installed with pnpm that also has `graphql@16` in its tree:

```js
const { GraphQLUtils } = require("@medusajs/framework/utils")
const { CacheInvalidationParser } = require("@medusajs/caching/dist/utils/parser")
new CacheInvalidationParser(
  GraphQLUtils.makeExecutableSchema({ typeDefs: "type Product { id: ID! }" }),
  []
)
```

```text
Error: Cannot use GraphQLObjectType "Product" from another module or realm.
```

In the running app the first visible symptom is any untagged set:

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parseObjectForEntities')
    at DefaultCacheStrategy.computeTags (@medusajs/caching/src/utils/strategy.ts:112:36)
    at CachingModuleService.set_ (@medusajs/caching/src/services/cache-module.ts:275:59)
    at CachingModuleService.set (@medusajs/caching/src/services/cache-module.ts:240:23)
```

## Suggested fix

Declare `"graphql": "^17.0.2"` (the same range as `@medusajs/utils`) in
`packages/modules/caching/package.json` `dependencies`. As a workaround, a pnpm
`packageExtensions` entry adding that dependency to `@medusajs/caching@2.22.4` fixes it.

It may also be worth logging the error `CachingModuleService.onApplicationStart` raises instead of
swallowing it, since the failure is otherwise invisible until the first `set`.

I can open the PR for the dependency declaration if a maintainer assigns this issue.

issue.title: [Bug]: User edit form silently swallows server errors (no toast, no message)
issue.body:
**What happened?**

When editing a user in the admin dashboard (Settings → Users → Edit) and the update request fails, there is no feedback at all. The drawer stays open, no toast, no error message. The only trace is an unhandled promise rejection in the browser console:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to fetch
```

Easy to reproduce: open the Edit User drawer, set DevTools → Network to "Offline" (or stop the backend), change the first name, click Save.

**Where the problem is:**

`edit-user-form.tsx` calls `mutateAsync` with only an `onSuccess` callback, `useUpdateUser` in `hooks/api/users.tsx` has no default `onError`, and there is no global MutationCache handler — so the rejection is silently dropped.

This is the same pattern as #17094 (collection edit form, fixed in #17112) and #17069 (promotion edit form, still open). The fix would mirror #17112: add an `onError` that shows the error in a toast.

I verified this on `develop` today. I'd like to be assigned — happy to open a PR following the same approach as #17112.

issue.title: fix(dashboard): keep list filters and page when going back through breadcrumbs
issue.body:
## What

Fixes a customer-reported issue in the admin dashboard: opening an order's details from the Orders list and going back via the topbar breadcrumb reset the list's search criteria, filters (such as the date filter), sorting and current page.

The order detail page has no "Back" button of its own; the way back to the list is the "Orders" breadcrumb in the shared topbar. `Breadcrumbs` built each crumb link from `match.pathname` alone (`<Link to={crumb.path}>`), and the Orders list keeps all of its state in URL search params (`q`, `offset`, `order`, `created_at`, ...), so the link went to plain `/orders` and every param was dropped. (The browser back button itself was not affected.)

## Why this approach

- Adds a small `useRememberedSearch` hook next to the shell: it records the last `location.search` seen for each pathname during the session, and `Breadcrumbs` uses it for its non-final crumb links (`to={withRememberedSearch(crumb.path)}`), so "Orders" now goes back to `/orders?<previous params>`.
- It builds on the dashboard's existing pattern of keeping params when navigating back (`useStateAwareTo` / `restore_params`, `export${location.search}` links) instead of introducing a new storage mechanism.
- Because the shared breadcrumb is fixed rather than an orders-only one, other list pages (products, customers, ...) also keep their filters when returning through the breadcrumb — same one-line root cause.
- If a list was never visited with params, the link is still the plain path. The remembered search lives only in memory for the session; sidebar navigation links are unchanged and still open lists without params.

## Changes

- `packages/admin/dashboard/src/components/layout/shell/shell.tsx` — breadcrumb links now reuse the last search string seen for that pathname

issue.title: fix(inventory): don't re-add reserved quantity when restoring live reservations
issue.body:
## Summary

**What** — Restoring reservations in the Inventory Module now only adds back the reserved quantity for reservations that were actually soft-deleted.

**Why** — `restoreReservationItems` and `restoreReservationItemsByLineItem` restored the rows, then re-listed every targeted reservation (live ones included) and added each quantity to the inventory level's `reserved_quantity`. Calling either method on a reservation that isn't deleted (custom code, or a compensation over ids that weren't all deleted) inflated `reserved_quantity` by the reservation's quantity on every call, which lowered the available quantity.

**How** — In `packages/modules/inventory/src/services/inventory-module.ts`, `restoreReservationItems_` and `restoreReservationItemsByLineItem_` now list the targeted reservations with `withDeleted: true` before restoring, keep only those with a `deleted_at`, and pass that set to `adjustInventoryLevelsForReservationsRestore`.

**Testing** — Added two cases to `packages/modules/inventory/integration-tests/__tests__/inventory-module-service.spec.ts`:
- Restoring a mix of one deleted and one live reservation twice: before the fix the levels ended at `reserved_quantity` 4 and 6; they now stay at 2 and 2.
- Restoring by line item when the reservations are live: before the fix `reserved_quantity` went from 6 to 10; it now stays at 6.

The full inventory module integration spec (38 tests) and the package unit suite pass.

issue.title: [Bug]: @medusajs/core-flows imports undeclared @medusajs/workflows-sdk and @medusajs/utils
issue.body:
### Package.json file
@medusajs/core-flows 2.21.2 (develop; first observed in the published 2.15.3 dist) — dependencies: csv-parse, deeks, json-2-csv; peerDependencies: @medusajs/framework

### Bug
A few files in `@medusajs/core-flows` import `@medusajs/workflows-sdk` / `@medusajs/utils` directly, while the package declares neither (everything else goes through `@medusajs/framework/*`):

- `src/cart/steps/validate-shipping.ts` → `@medusajs/workflows-sdk`
- `src/cart/steps/validate-shipping-methods-data.ts` → `@medusajs/workflows-sdk`
- `src/common/steps/use-query-graph.ts` → `@medusajs/workflows-sdk`, `@medusajs/utils`
- `src/payment/workflows/process-payment.ts` → `@medusajs/utils`, `@medusajs/workflows-sdk`
- `src/order/workflows/transfer/request-order-transfer.ts` → `@medusajs/utils`
- `src/order/workflows/transfer/accept-order-transfer.ts` → `@medusajs/utils`

(In 2.15.3 the same list also included `product/steps/normalize-products-to-chunks.js`, which has since been fixed on develop.)

They only resolve when the package manager happens to hoist those packages. With pnpm, hoisting is skipped once two versions are present (for example right after upgrading 2.15.2 → 2.15.3 without wiping `node_modules`), and then:

- `medusa develop` fails with `Error: Cannot find module '@medusajs/workflows-sdk'` (require stack in `@medusajs/core-flows/dist/...`), or
- `POST /store/carts` returns 500: `TypeError: undefined is not a function` in `create-cart -> update-cart-promotions-as-step (invoke)`.

Same error as #13043 (closed); these imports are still there in 2.21.2.

### Expected
core-flows resolves with only its declared dependencies (`@medusajs/framework`).

### Fix
Import through `@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk` and `@medusajs/framework/utils`, like the rest of the package. PR: #17120

issue.title: fix(core-flows): validate that customer email matches the authenticated auth identity
issue.body:
## Summary

**What** — `createCustomerAccountWorkflow` (used by `POST /store/customers`) now checks that the customer email matches the email of the auth identity it is attached to. A mismatch is rejected with a 400 `invalid_data` error.

**Why** — The route passes the request-body email and `auth_context.auth_identity_id` to the workflow (`packages/medusa/src/api/store/customers/route.ts:26-31`). The workflow's validation step only checked that an email was present and looked for existing customers. It never loaded the auth identity, so the body email was stored as-is. An auth identity registered for one email could create an account-holding customer for a different email, which can lead to account squatting and guest orders being matched to the wrong customer by email.

**How**
- `packages/core/core-flows/src/customer/steps/validate-customer-account-creation.ts`
  - When `authIdentityId` is set, the step loads the auth identity with `provider_identities`.
  - It collects the identity's emails: `entity_id` for the `emailpass` provider, and `user_metadata.email` for any provider (Google, GitHub, and others).
  - If it finds any emails and none match the body email (case-insensitive), it throws `MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA`.
  - On a match, the step returns the auth identity's email, and the existing duplicate checks run against that email.
  - Identities without an email skip the check, e.g. GitHub with a private email or custom providers.
- `packages/core/core-flows/src/customer/workflows/create-customer-account.ts` creates the customer with the email returned by the step.

## Testing

5 tests added to `integration-tests/http/__tests__/customer/store/customer.spec.ts`:
- Mismatched emailpass email → 400, and no customer is created (failed before the fix).
- Emails that differ only in casing → the customer is created with the auth identity's email (failed before the fix).
- Workflow with a social identity whose `user_metadata.email` doesn't match → error (failed before the fix).
- Matching social `user_metadata.email` → created (passes before and after).
- Identity with no email → created (passes before and after).

After the fix:
- The store customer spec passes 12/12.
- Other suites that call `POST /store/customers` pass 59/59: `customer/admin/customer.spec.ts`, `auth/emailpass-actor-association.spec.ts`, `auth/admin/auth.spec.ts`, `order/admin/transfer-flow.spec.ts`.
- `@medusajs/core-flows` unit tests pass 31/31, `tsc --noEmit` and eslint are clean.

## Behavior changes

- Callers of `createCustomerAccountWorkflow` that attach an emailpass or social identity to a customer with a different email now get an error.
- When emails differ only in casing, the auth identity's casing is stored.
- The step now returns `{ email }`; before, it returned nothing.

## Known limits

- The emailpass `entity_id` is only used as an email when the provider identity's `provider` is `"emailpass"`; a custom provider that stores the email only in `entity_id` is not checked unless it also sets `user_metadata.email`.

Closes DX-3139

issue.title: [Bug]: Caching module invalidation is unbounded and runs on `worker_mode: server` processes, OOMing the API container under bulk writes
issue.body:
### Package.json file

```JSON
 Relevant versions: `@medusajs/medusa` / `@medusajs/framework` 2.19.0, `@medusajs/caching-redis` ^2.19.0, `@medusajs/event-bus-redis` ^2.19.0.
```

### Node.js version

v22.18.0

### Database and its version

PostgreSQL 16.2

### Operating system name and version

Debian 12 (node:22-slim container), Linux host

### Browser name

_No response_

### What happended?


The Caching Module's automatic invalidation has two independent problems. Together they exhaust the Node heap of a self-hosted deployment during any burst of writes — in our case a catalogue sync through the Admin API, which killed the API container roughly 90 seconds after every boot.

**1. Clears are dispatched with `void`, so nothing can apply backpressure.**

`CachingModuleService.performCacheClear` (`dist/services/cache-module.js`, `src/services/cache-module.ts`):

```js
for (const providerId of providerIds_) {
  const provider = this.providerService.retrieveProvider(providerId);
  void provider.clear({ key, tags, options });   // <-- not awaited
}
```

Because of the `void`, the `await` in `clear_` resolves before Redis has done anything, and the `ongoingRequests` coalescing above it can never dedupe — the entry is deleted almost immediately. `performCacheSet` does the same with `provider.set(...)`.

For the `caching-redis` provider, one tag-based `clear` is an `SMEMBERS` per tag, then a `getBuffer` per member key under `Promise.all`. With a hot list tag such as `Product:list:*`, that set contains one member per cached list key. So each call materialises thousands of buffers, and N concurrent calls materialise N × that, with nothing limiting N.

**2. The invalidation handler is registered as an event-bus interceptor, so it runs in the emitting process.**

`DefaultCacheStrategy.onApplicationStart` (`dist/utils/strategy.js`, `src/utils/strategy.ts`):

```js
eventBus.subscribe("*", handleEvent);
eventBus.addInterceptor?.(handleEvent);
```

`subscribe` only runs where the BullMQ worker exists — `event-bus-redis` builds a worker only `if (this.isWorkerMode)`. But `addInterceptor` runs wherever an event is *emitted*: `RedisEventBusService.emit()` calls `eventsToEmit.forEach((eventData) => this.callInterceptors(eventData, ...))`, and `releaseGroupedEvents()` does the same. `AbstractEventBusModuleService.callInterceptors` maps over the handlers without awaiting them.

So a process started with `projectConfig.workerMode: "server"` — which is documented as not processing events — runs the full invalidation for every event it emits, i.e. for every write served by the Admin/Store API, while also serving HTTP traffic.

**3. The interceptor is also redundant.** In both `emit()` and `releaseGroupedEvents()`, every event is queued to BullMQ whenever a matching subscriber exists, and the strategy's own `subscribe("*")` guarantees the wildcard filter matches. So in a server/worker split, each event is invalidated twice: once in-process on the server via the interceptor, once on the worker via the queue.


### Expected behavior


- `worker_mode: "server"` processes do not run cache invalidation, or the interceptor path is reconciled with the `*` subscriber so each event is invalidated exactly once.
- Invalidation applies backpressure: `provider.clear(...)` is awaited (which also makes the existing `ongoingRequests` coalescing effective), and/or tags from a burst of events are batched into a bounded number of clears instead of one clear per event.

### Actual behavior

Under a bulk write burst (~10k products updated through the Admin API), the `server` container's heap climbs continuously and V8 aborts:

```
<--- Last few GCs --->
[20:0x31b25000]    88305 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 2023.7 (2075.3) -> 2021.1 (2076.5) MB, ...
[20:0x31b25000]    88629 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 2024.8 (2076.5) -> 2023.5 (2096.8) MB, ...
<--- JS stacktrace --->
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

Secondary symptoms before the crash:

- Unrelated request latency degrades from ~10 ms to 7.6 s as the event loop starves.
- The clears exceed `caching-redis`'s default 5 s `commandTimeout`. That is caught by `isConnectionError` and returned as a no-op, so invalidation aborts half-done: stale entries stay cached and their key names remain as orphaned members of the tag set, making every subsequent clear of that tag more expensive.

Setting `workerMode: "server"` does not avoid it, and there is no option to disable automatic invalidation — the `caching` feature flag only gates whether anything is *stored* (`useCache` / `@Cached`), while `onApplicationStart` wires invalidation unconditionally. Not registering the module at all is the only supported way to silence it, which also gives up caching.

Custom strategies would be the natural escape hatch, but they are currently disabled in `loaders/providers.js`:

```js
const strategy = strategy_1.DefaultCacheStrategy; // Re enable custom strategy another time
```

A `patch-package` patch against 2.19.0, if useful as a starting point:

1. `await provider.clear(...)` in `performCacheClear` instead of `void`.
2. Drop the `addInterceptor` registration (redundant with the `*` subscriber, per point 3).
3. Accumulate tags from events into a deduplicating `Set`, drained by one flush at a time in batches. In our workload the tags across a sync are nearly all duplicates, so tens of thousands of events collapse into a handful of clears.

After this, the same sync runs flat instead of OOMing.
